# 🗓️ Meeting Notes Template

> Record decisions and actionable work. Do not include passwords, access tokens, private personal data, or confidential vulnerability details.

## 1. Meeting metadata

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Meeting title | |
| Date | |
| Start/end time and timezone | |
| Facilitator | |
| Note taker | |
| Participants | |
| Meeting type | Planning / design review / incident review / release review / other |
| Related issue or PR | |

## 2. Purpose and expected outcome

State why the meeting is needed and what decision or output should result. Identify topics explicitly out of scope.

## 3. Agenda

| Order | Topic | Presenter/owner | Desired outcome | Timebox |
|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| 1 | | | | |
| 2 | | | | |
| 3 | | | | |

## 4. Discussion notes

For each topic record:
- Context and current behavior.
- Options considered.
- Evidence, examples or test results.
- Constraints and assumptions.
- Risks and unanswered questions.

Separate confirmed facts from proposals and opinions.

## 5. Decisions

| Decision ID | Decision | Rationale | Decision owner | Related ADR/issue |
|---|---|---|---|---|

If a decision changes architecture or user-visible behavior, create or update an ADR. Meeting notes do not replace the ADR.

## 6. Action items

| Action | Owner | Priority | Due date/timezone | Completion evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Every action should have one accountable owner and a verifiable completion condition.

## 7. Risks and blockers

| Risk/blocker | Impact | Mitigation/next step | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|

## 8. Follow-up

- Next meeting:
- Required preparation:
- People to notify:
- Open questions:

## 9. References

Link relevant repository issues, pull requests, CI runs, source commits, ADRs and documentation. Store sensitive incident details in the appropriate private reporting channel rather than this public template.
